comparisons.peer_topic: Home Equity Portfolio Composition and Trends
comparisons.peer_summary: The home equity portfolio constituted 6% of the consumer portfolio at year-end 2024, with outstanding balances increasing by $210 million to $25.7 billion primarily due to draws and new originations outpacing paydowns. The company no longer originates home equity loans or reverse mortgages.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose the size and composition of their home equity portfolios, specifically highlighting HELOCs. JPMorgan reports a retained HELOC carrying value of $14.5 billion, noting that $3.8 billion had recast or been modified. In contrast, Bank of America reports a broader home equity portfolio of $25.7 billion (including HELOCs, loans, and reverse mortgages), with only 9% of the total requiring interest-only payments. While JPMorgan explicitly details the modification/recast activity within its HELOCs, Bank of America focuses on the overall portfolio growth driven by draws outpacing paydowns and notes it no longer originates new home equity loans or reverse mortgages.

sentences.text: The carrying value of retained home equity lines of credit outstanding was $14.5 billion at December 31, 2024, including $3.8 billion of HELOCs that have recast from interest-only to fully amortizing payments or have been modified, and $3.6 billion of interest-only balloon HELOCs, which primarily mature after 2030.
At December 31, 2024, the home equity portfolio made up six percent of the consumer portfolio and was comprised of home equity lines of credit (HELOCs), home equity loans and reverse mortgages.
Of the $25.7 billion in total home equity portfolio outstandings at December 31, 2024, as shown in Table 23, nine percent require interest-only payments.

comparisons.peer_topic: Residential Real Estate Loan Types and Portfolio Status
comparisons.peer_summary: Residential real estate loans consist of first- and second-lien mortgages, including HELOCs, the vast majority of which are held for investment in the Wealth Management business segment's loan portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley identify HELOCs as a component of their residential real estate lending. JPMorgan manages HELOC risk during the revolving period by reducing or canceling undrawn lines in response to creditworthiness declines or property value decreases. Morgan Stanley categorizes HELOCs within its residential real estate loans, noting they are primarily held for investment in its Wealth Management segment, but does not provide specific portfolio values or risk management actions for HELOCs in the same detailed manner as JPMorgan.

sentences.text: The Firm manages the risk of HELOCs during their revolving period by reducing or canceling the undrawn line in accordance with the contract or to the extent otherwise permitted by law, including when there has been a demonstrable decline in the creditworthiness of the borrower or significant decrease in the value of the underlying property.
Residential real estate loans consist of first- and second-lien mortgages, including HELOCs.
